answer: Under adversarial multi-agent environments, dynamic opportunity-cost bonds scaled to the resource zenith and backed by subgame-perfect punishment matrices guarantee a strict Nash equilibrium: identity multiplication yields strictly negative payoff because each Sybil must post collateral proportional to marginal extraction, rendering the expected attack cost above the attainable shale-level rent ceiling. Since the equilibrium kernel bounds every deviation by a profitable unilateral defection, Sybil strategies collapse.
